title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E443 treats the transverse vibrations of an elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam) of length a. For the clamped–free (cantilever) case the frequency condition is 2 = −cos Φ (e^Φ + e^{−Φ}), i.e. cos Φ cosh Φ = −1. Here Φ is the dimensionless eigenvalue, the modern βL.

Method. Euler sets Φ = (2n−1)ρ ± ω with ρ = π/2 and ω small. He uses common logarithms of e^π, e^{π/2} and so on (previous page), then expands e^{±ω}, sin ω and cos ω in power series. This turns the transcendental equation into a polynomial in ω.

First root (previous page): ω = 0.30432, so Φ1 = 1.87511.

Second root (this page). Put Φ = 3π/2 − ω. With A = e^{3π/2} ≈ 111.3178 and B = e^{−3π/2} ≈ 0.008983 the equation becomes 2 = sin ω (A e^{−ω} + B e^{ω}). Expanding gives 2 = (A+B)ω − (A−B)ω² + (A+B)/3·ω³. The coefficients are 111.32669, 111.30871 and 37.10890, exactly as printed. Its root is ω ≈ 0.01830; Euler gives 0.01829, so Φ2 = 4.69408 (modern 4.694091).

Higher roots. Since ω ≈ 2e^{−Φ}, Euler states that ω may be neglected and Φ ≈ 5ρ, 7ρ, 9ρ, … i.e. (2n−1)π/2. This is the standard asymptotic form of the cantilever eigenvalues. The table nevertheless lists corrected values: 7.85473 (true 7.854757), 10.99553 (true 10.995541), 14.13711 (true 14.137168).

Table (§XVIII).
- Vibration times are T = π a²/(Φ² b²).
- 'Sounds' (frequencies) are 1/T = Φ² b²/(π a²).
- b⁴ = 2hk c², where h is the fall height in one second (15 5/8 Rhenish feet) and kc² is the elastic constant (flexural rigidity per unit weight). It is to be measured by a static cantilever-deflection experiment, set up in §XIX and continued on the next page.
- The problem served: predicting the absolute and relative pitches of a clamped vibrating lamina. Overtone ratios are Φn²/Φ1² = 1 : 6.267 : 17.55 : 34.39 : …, which are inharmonic.
errors: Inconsistency between pages for the first root. The previous page gives Φ1 = 1.87511, the table 1.87514. True value 1.875104; ρ + 0.30432 = 1.875116.
Second root: ω more precisely 0.018298, so Φ2 = 4.694091 rather than 4.69408 (minor).

Fourth row: the vibration time 0.02493 is wrong. π/10.99553² = 0.025985, so the 'sound' should be ≈ 38.484, not 40.1107. Euler's 40.1107 is consistent with his wrong time (1/0.02493 ≈ 40.11) but not with Φ.
Second row: the sound 6.9977 should be 1/0.14258 = Φ²/π ≈ 7.0138. The third row (19.6388) is computed correctly, which confirms the intended formula.
Fifth row: Φ5 = 14.13711 should be 14.13717. The sound 63.5439 should be Φ²/π ≈ 63.617 with Euler's own Φ (≈ 63.62 with the true root). The time 0.01573 is about right (0.01572).

Text/table mismatch: the text says ω may be 'penitus' neglected for higher roots (Φ = 5ρ, 7ρ, …), yet the tabulated values include the small corrections. With pure (2n−1)π/2 one would get 7.85398 etc.

ideas.what: Numerical solution of the cantilever frequency equation cos Φ cosh Φ = −1 by perturbation about (2n−1)π/2 with series expansion in ω
ideas.modern_name: Eigenvalues βnL of the clamped–free Euler–Bernoulli beam; perturbative root-finding
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744, Additamentum 'De curvis elasticis' to the Methodus inveniendi) and Daniel Bernoulli (1742–1751)
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum I (1744); E443 itself; discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11₂)

ideas.what: Asymptotic law Φn ≈ (2n−1)π/2 with exponentially small correction ω ≈ ±2e^{−Φ}
ideas.modern_name: Asymptotic eigenvalues of the cantilever beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler / D. Bernoulli; standard in Rayleigh's Theory of Sound

ideas.what: Absolute frequencies ∝ Φ² b²/a², with b⁴ fixed by gravity and a static deflection measurement of the flexural constant
ideas.modern_name: Natural frequencies ω_n = (βnL)² √(EI/ρA)/L², with calibration of EI from static cantilever deflection
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler; Daniel Bernoulli for experimental pitch comparison

deep.surprise_reason: Standard cantilever eigenvalue computation already known from Euler 1744 and Bernoulli. The only noteworthy items are arithmetic slips in the table (4th row time and sound, 2nd and 5th sounds). These are minor and possibly already noted by the Opera omnia editors (unsure).
transcription_corrections: 'ω = 0,01829' in the image has a stray ink mark after '=' that is not a digit; the value is 0,01829.
Exponent in the second equation: the image's last term reads ω^3 (printed blurred, looks like ω^5); the computation confirms ω³.
Table entries are transcribed faithfully. 0,02493 and 40,1107 are as printed (Euler's errors, not OCR errors).
